summary: Created a "Fleet Internal CA" on node1, issued and installed a CA-signed TLS certificate (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.96.11) for node2, configured node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with that certificate (via a systemd-managed openssl s_server unit, since no package repos were available to install httpd/nginx), opened the port in firewalld, and installed the Fleet Internal CA as a trusted system CA on both node1 and node2 via update-ca-trust. Verified trust end-to-end with curl (no -k) and openssl s_client returning Verify return code: 0. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of CA trust and the HTTPS service.
actions_performed: Generated 4096-bit CA key and self-signed 'Fleet Internal CA' certificate on node1 (/etc/pki/fleet-ca/) and installed it into node1's system trust store via update-ca-trust
Generated node2 private key and CSR (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2 / IP:10.100.96.11) on node2
Signed node2's CSR with the Fleet Internal CA on node1, producing a server cert with SAN and serverAuth EKU
Installed the Fleet Internal CA cert and signed node2 cert on node2; built a fullchain cert; installed the CA into node2's system trust store

Configured node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using an openssl s_server-based systemd service (fleet-tls.service, enabled and persistent) since no local/offline package repo existed to install httpd/nginx
Opened TCP/8443 in node2's firewalld public zone (permanent)
Verified trusted HTTPS from node1 to node2 with curl (no -k) and openssl s_client (Verify return code 0)
Captured baseline boot IDs and health for both nodes
Restarted node1 then node2 one at a time via systemd-run scheduled reboot, polled until each came back, confirmed changed boot IDs
Re-verified CA trust and HTTPS service health on both nodes post-restart
Cleaned up the transient one-shot reboot timer/service units on both nodes

evidence.requirement: Create CA 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
evidence.summary: CA key and self-signed cert generated on node1 with subject/issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA, 10-year validity
CSR generated on node2 (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.96.11), signed by Fleet Internal CA on node1, cert verified OK against CA

evidence.requirement: Configure node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with that certificate
evidence.summary: fleet-tls.service (openssl s_server) installed, enabled, listening on 8443 after firewalld port opened; curl from node1 without -k returns HTTP 200 with issuer=Fleet Internal CA and TLS verify OK

evidence.requirement: Install CA as trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: update-ca-trust extract run on node1; trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor/authority both before and after restart

evidence.requirement: Install CA as trusted system CA on node2
evidence.summary: CA cert written to node2 anchors and update-ca-trust extract run; trust list and openssl verify against system bundle confirm anchor status
Captured boot_id c8eba47a... and confirmed Fleet Internal CA trust anchor present pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled reboot acknowledged immediately; node became unreachable mid-restart; boot_id changed from c8eba47a... to 720679e7... confirming actual restart
Post-restart: Fleet Internal CA still trust anchor, CA cert readable, and TLS fetch to node2 (HTTP 200, verify 0) confirms node1's trust store and network function correctly after reboot
Captured boot_id 151c4aa9..., fleet-tls.service active/enabled, listening on 8443, curl to service succeeded pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled reboot acknowledged; node briefly unreachable; boot_id changed from 151c4aa9... to 49ce85f3... confirming actual restart

Post-restart: fleet-tls.service active/enabled and listening on 8443 again, Fleet Internal CA still trust anchor, local and remote (from node1) HTTPS fetches succeed with TLS verify OK, confirming service and cert survived reboot
